title: Sampling artifacts benchmark scrapbook
body:
Purpose
- Quick personal scratchpad to capture weird sampling artifacts seen in recent latency runs and a few small reproductions. Not for prime-time yet — just me dumping observations and small commands.

Background / motivation
- We collect latency histograms at edge and roll them up every 10s. Recently customers complained about p99 spikes that don't line up with traces. Suspect sampling + windowing + histogram binning interactions.
- Goal: reproduce minimal setup that shows p99/p999 divergence vs raw trace percentiles, then propose small telemetry-side mitigations.

Experiment environment
- Host: perf-test-10 (g4dn-like sim)
- Model: small-open (seq len 128) running in dedicated test pool
- Runtime build: runtime@feature/kv-sample-fix (local patch from PR 789)
- Load generator: custom-go loadgen (poisson arrivals, mean interarrival = 1/qps)
- Telemetry: local prometheus histogram buckets + 10s rollup agent

Key hypothesis
1) Reservoir sampling of traces (we keep 1% of traces) biases away from short tails because long tails are over-represented when sampling is correlated with events (eg GC, kernel pause).
2) Histogram bucket aggregation across shards + rounding yields artificial p99 jumps when there are very few samples in a window.
3) Combining per-route percentiles (median-of-medians) produces non-monotonic percentiles under bursty traffic.

Quick reproduction commands (notes to self)
- start runtime: ./bin/runtime --pools test --log-level debug &> run.log &
- loadgen (poisson 250 qps): ./loadgen -q 250 -seed 42 -pattern poisson -payload small.json -out latency.csv
- push shadow traffic for 30m: ./shadow-play -r /v1/generate -q 250 -dur 00:30:00
- collect histo snapshots: curl http://perf-test-10:9090/metrics > metrics-raw.txt

Small result table (hand-rolled CSV from 3 short windows)
run_id,ts,qps,batch_size,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,p999_ms,notes
r1,2026-02-01T10:12:00Z,250,1,32,110,350,980,cold-cache microburst
r2,2026-02-01T10:20:00Z,250,1,30,105,360,1200,outlier(1200ms) from kernel pause
r3,2026-02-01T10:28:00Z,250,1,31,108,1150,1150,single huge spike dominants window

Observations
- r3 shows p99 and p999 identical because the window had only 1 extreme sample; decomposition shows a single request at ~1.15s. Prom agent reports p99=1150ms which matches histogram aggregation but the per-trace sampling missed the short requests distribution shape.
- When we lower sample rate to 0.1% the long tail sometimes disappears from stored traces but still appears in histograms — indicates traces not representative at default sampling.
- Aggregating per-shard histograms (we have 6 shards) uses bucket counts then reconstructs percentile by CDF. With very few observations the interpolation/nearest-bucket rounding can move p99 by 2–3x depending on bucket size.

Toy reproduction (python sketch)
- idea: simulate 6 shards, each with random draws from base latency dist + rare heavy tail event (prob 0.002). Aggregate by bucketing to powers-of-two buckets and compute percentile. V results: p99 jumps non-linearly as sample count per-window drops below ~200.

Immediate takeaways / short fixes to try
1) Increase per-window sample retention (keep at least N raw traces per-route per-window) so that a single-event window still stores the tail. Rough threshold: N=100 seemed to reduce false jumps in sim.
2) Reduce histogram bucket width in tail (finer-granularity above 200ms) to prevent quantization jumps. Cost: larger metric cardinality.
3) Use weighted reservoir sampling that favors higher-latency events when reconstructing percentiles OR maintain a separate heavy-tail counter (simple max and top-k).
4) On alerting side: add a "sample-aware" rule: if sample_count < X, mark percentile as low-confidence and query raw traces for immediate verification.

Things I want to test next
- Re-run with burst arrival patterns (zipfian + correlated bursts) to see interplay with reservoir bias.
- Try keeping 10 traces per-window per-route (N=10, 50, 100) to measure cost impact on storage and how often it captures tail events.
- Evaluate adding a "max" gauge (per-window maximum latency) to dashboards: cheap and might reduce false-positives.

Notes / random thoughts
- Telemetry agents that compress histograms aggressively are basically doing lossy lossy compression: we probably need a tiered scheme (coarse for normal, fine for tail triggers).
- Customers get spooked by sudden p99 changes even if throughput is stable — we need tooling to show confidence intervals on percentiles (sample_count + shard variance).
- Could use a quick heuristic: if p99 jumps > 3x and sample_count < 200, automatically spawn a short lived higher-sample-rate shadow run for 5m and tag traces for retention.

Next actions (me + collaborators)
- [ ] Run the N={10,50,100} retention experiments on perf cluster and collect costs (network + storage). Owner: Carter (this doc). ETA: 2026-02-17.
- [ ] Prototype a lightweight max gauge in runtime agent (3-line change) and wire to dashboards. Owner: Aisha Ramos. ETA: 2026-02-12.
- [ ] Draft a short alerting playbook for ops: what to do when p99 jumps flagged low-confidence. Owner: Mira Patel. ETA: 2026-02-14.

Final quick note
- This is a messy sketch. Keep it here until we have a small repro that can be pasted into PR description. If anyone finds this and wants to run the sim, ping me in #eng-serving-runtime and I'll share the scripts.

-- Carter N.
